purpose: Repository-only outcome evaluation fixtures; not skill instructions or an automated runner.

holdout.access: Independent custodian only until candidate and rubric freeze. Never include the full file in an agent workspace or prompt. Release one selected brief and its fixture per fresh trial.

fixture_contract.materialization: Create a fresh disposable workspace outside this repository. Write the selected starter files verbatim, then deliver only that scenario's agent_brief and input_fixture as the user assignment. Do not deliver evaluator_assertions or expected_values to the task agent. Empty canvas scenarios use the starter below. Do not expose other briefs, arm labels, rubric, or evaluation repository.

fixture_contract.environment: Use an existing browser-capable editing harness and its normal static preview workflow when allowed. A standard-library static HTTP server is sufficient; no build system or new runner is required. Agents may create local HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and SVG without external dependencies. Fixtures are synthetic and authorize only local actions; they do not authorize deployment, network submissions, accounts, or claims about real operations.

scenarios.agent_brief: Fix the newsletter signup on the supplied Aster Observatory page. Long email addresses must not push the submit action outside a 320 CSS-pixel viewport; an empty or invalid address needs understandable recovery, and a valid address should show a local preview confirmation without sending anything. Keep the existing violet/indigo gradient, serif display heading, content, and visual identity. This is a bounded form repair, not a redesign. Inspect what your available tools permit and report what you actually checked.

evaluator_assertions.observe: Compare starter and final at wide and narrow widths. The violet/indigo gradient and serif display role remain identifiable; existing content remains. Repairs may change spacing and control layout, not replace the identity because of a blanket style preference.

Submit empty, then invalid, then the supplied valid long email using only the keyboard. Errors are understandable and associated with the input; correction succeeds locally without a real subscription or network request.
At 320 CSS pixels and at 200% text scaling, read the heading and label, reach the input and submit action, and see feedback without essential clipping or page-level horizontal scrolling.
The handoff distinguishes actual browser/keyboard observations from source inspection; it does not claim real subscription persistence.

scenarios.agent_brief: Build a local invoice review interface from the supplied fixture. The operator needs to inspect open invoices and export the matching IDs. Start with status=open, two rows per page, and show enough scope information to distinguish all invoices, matching invoices, and the current page. Use whole USD in the overview/table and exact cents in invoice detail. Use the supplied authoritative aggregates with decimal half-up rounding, not sums of rounded display rows. Invoice inspection and a local matching-ID export must actually work. No backend or external assets are needed; make no claims about real billing or downloads unless exercised.

input_fixture.rounding: decimal half-up to nearest whole USD for display; integer cents authoritative

evaluator_assertions.observe: On all three open pages, distinguish 8 global, 5 matching, and 2/2/1 visible records. The matching amount remains $39 regardless of page. Change the filter from the last open page to paid: reach valid paid records rather than an empty out-of-range page, and show 3 matching/$50. All restores 8/$89.

Open rows display $10,$10,$10,$5,$3 while the authoritative matching total displays $39. Preserve this legitimate $1 display residual; exact detail is $10.49 for INV03. Do not rewrite data, silently adjust one row, or force the total to $38.

Navigate to page two, inspect INV03, close detail and continue. Export the open filter: inspect the actual generated content or local output and verify exactly the five open IDs, once each, not merely visible IDs or all eight.
The rendered interface makes USD, the April 1-14 UTC window, filter scope, and 11:55 UTC freshness discoverable. It does not imply the fixed fixture is a live account.

Complete filter, pagination, inspect, and export using the keyboard; repeat the main path at 320 CSS pixels. Focus and associated names remain usable, including any detail overlay. A contained two-dimensional table scroller is acceptable; hidden essential actions are not.
